context: A color palette accessibility tool with three panels: a bar chart previewing the active palette, a 7x7 WCAG contrast ratio matrix between all palette color pairs, and CVD simulation strips showing how the palette appears under protanopia, deuteranopia, and tritanopia.
first_impression: Clean, purposeful three-panel layout that packages complementary accessibility views without feeling crowded.
what_works: Traffic-light encoding (green/yellow/red) in the contrast matrix makes pass/fail status scannable at a glance without reading numbers; the four-column CVD strip layout enables direct side-by-side comparison of vision types with minimal eye travel.
what_doesnt: Hex labels in the CVD strips are rendered at 6.5px and are effectively unreadable in the screenshot, adding visual clutter with no payoff; the contrast matrix is nearly all red because palette-to-palette contrast predictably fails WCAG AA, which may confuse viewers who expect the tool to surface actionable failures rather than expected ones.
